Nihari is a story that starts in the lanes of Shahjahanabad, travels through Awadh's royal kitchens, crosses the border in 1947, and still finds its way to Friday morning tables across the subcontinent.
In this episode of Khana Dil Se, we trace the history of one of India's most beloved slow-cooked dishes - from coal fires after Fajar namaaz to pressure cookers on gas burners.
You could make Nihari at home - mutton or vegetarian, with Khamiri Roti on the side. No secret formula, just patience, the right spices, and a little faith.

For the Nihari
